source: FRC Vision (Limelight / PhotonVision / custom) — research dossier for PumpkinLib, August 2026
summary: As of Aug 2026 the FRC vision stack has consolidated around two vendor products (Limelight OS 2026.1 with LimelightHelpers/LimelightLib, and PhotonVision 2026.3.4 with photonlib) plus a small but influential tier of homebrew coprocessor pipelines (6328's Northstar, Team 190's GompeiVision, 1701's CubVision) that publish raw double arrays over NT4. Both vendors now converge on the same conceptual output — a field-relative Pose3d with a capture-time timestamp, a tag count, an average tag distance, and an ambiguity — but expose it through completely incompatible APIs (Limelight: flat `botpose_orb_wpiblue` double[] on NetworkTables, gyro-fed MegaTag2, camera transform configured in the web UI; PhotonVision: `PhotonCamera.getAllUnreadResults()` returning `PhotonPipelineResult` with `multitagResult`, camera transform configured in robot code). PhotonVision 2026 deprecated the entire `PoseStrategy` enum + `PhotonPoseEstimator.update()` in favor of explicit `estimateCoprocMultiTagPose(result)` / `estimateLowestAmbiguityPose(result)` / `estimatePnpDistanceTrigSolvePose(result)` / `estimateConstrainedSolvepnpPose(...)` methods — a breaking-ish change most 2025 tutorials have not caught up with. The 2026 REBUILT field ships two layouts (`AprilTagFields.k2026RebuiltWelded`, `k2026RebuiltAndymark`) and mismatching them between coprocessor and robot code is still the single most common silent pose-estimation bug. The de-facto reference integration is the AdvantageKit vision template's `VisionIO`/`PoseObservation` abstraction, which already unifies Limelight MegaTag1, MegaTag2 and PhotonVision behind one record — PumpkinLib should adopt that shape, generalize it to custom sources and object detection, and add the things it lacks (a pluggable filter chain with reject reasons, a pluggable std-dev model, sim wiring for Limelight, a tag-layout override loader for WPIcal output, and vision-driven action commands). The big 2027 signal: WPILib 2027 renames all Java packages from `edu.wpi.first.*` to `org.wpilib.*`, drops NT3, and moves to Systemcore/Java 25 — AdvantageKit's main-branch templates are already written against `org.wpilib.*`, so PumpkinLib must keep vendor-facing code behind a thin seam or plan a mechanical rename.

landscape.tool: Limelight OS 2026 (LL4 / LL3G / LL3A / LL3 / LL2+)
landscape.doesWell: Zero-code AprilTag localization. MegaTag2 (`botpose_orb_wpiblue`) is ambiguity-free at any distance given a known yaw, and is the single best out-of-box localizer for a small team. LL4 has an internal IMU with 5 fusion modes (0 EXTERNAL_ONLY, 1 EXTERNAL_SEED, 2 INTERNAL_ONLY, 3 INTERNAL_MT1_ASSIST, 4 INTERNAL_EXTERNAL_ASSIST — mode 4 recommended). 2026.1 adds `tdist` (3D distance to target/POI), map POI offsets so all six Hub tags aim at Hub center, Hailo-8L default detector model, Hailo-accelerated AprilTags (up to 50% faster at 1x downscale), zero-shot classification, learning-based OCR (`rawocr`), neural detector clustering, WebRTC/H.264 streaming (46-91% bandwidth reduction). 2026.0 adds Rewind (.rwnd synchronized video+targeting+config capture, LL4 only), rebuilt ChArUco calibration workflow (~3x more detected corners), middle-of-exposure capture timestamps, free H100-backed neural net trainer at tools.limelightvision.io, skewed/perspective crop windows, NaN guards on all NT/JSON outputs. Sensors: LL4 and LL3G = OV9281 mono global shutter, 120FPS @ 1280x800 (LL3G also 240fps @ 640x480), FOV H:82° V:56.2°; LL3A/LL3 = OV5647 color rolling shutter.
landscape.gaps: Closed source. Camera-to-robot transform lives in the web UI / `camerapose_robotspace_set`, not in robot code — so it is invisible to sim and to AdvantageKit replay unless you mirror it. No first-party WPILib simulation path at all. MegaTag2 hard-requires `SetRobotOrientation` every frame or you get garbage. Pipeline switching is not instantaneous and there is no documented settle API — you must gate on `getCurrentPipelineIndex`/`getpipe` matching your request. LL4 dropped PoE (5V-26V buck-boost, 12W max), so wiring differs from LL3. `botpose` array packing is positional and undocumented in the LimelightHelpers Javadoc — you must read source. Latency accounting: the total latency is index 6 of the botpose array in ms, and `tl`+`cl` are separate keys; getting this wrong shifts your pose by 50-100ms of robot motion.

landscape.gaps: `getBotPoseEstimate_*` only returns the latest sample — it drops frames when the camera runs faster than the 50Hz robot loop. `getLatestResults()` does a full JSON parse on the RIO and is expensive; never call it in a hot loop. Method naming is inconsistent (`setPipelineIndex` lowercase vs `SetRobotOrientation` uppercase). No per-camera `Transform3d` accessor for sim.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should vendor LimelightHelpers verbatim as `org.pumpkinlib.vision.limelight.LimelightHelpers` (MIT-ish single file) so teams don't have to copy it, but implement the hot path over raw NT `readQueue()` as above so no frames are dropped.

landscape.doesWell: Open source, per-camera calibration you control, `Transform3d` robot-to-camera lives in robot code (so sim and replay are honest), and 8 selectable pose strategies. Verified `PhotonCamera` API: `PhotonCamera(String)`, `PhotonCamera(NetworkTableInstance,String)`, `List<PhotonPipelineResult> getAllUnreadResults()`, `@Deprecated PhotonPipelineResult getLatestResult()`, `boolean isConnected()`, `int getPipelineIndex()/setPipelineIndex(int)`, `int getFPSLimit()/setFPSLimit(int)`, `Optional<Matrix<N3,N3>> getCameraMatrix()`, `Optional<Matrix<N8,N1>> getDistCoeffs()`, `setDriverMode/getDriverMode`, `setLED(VisionLEDMode)`, `takeInputSnapshot/takeOutputSnapshot`, `getCameraTable()`, `static setVersionCheckEnabled(boolean)`; implements AutoCloseable. `PhotonPipelineResult` public fields: `PhotonPipelineMetadata metadata`, `List<PhotonTrackedTarget> targets`, `Optional<MultiTargetPNPResult> multitagResult`; methods `hasTargets()`, `getTargets()`, `getBestTarget()`, `getMultiTagResult()`, `double getTimestampSeconds()`. `PhotonTrackedTarget` public fields: `yaw, pitch, area, skew, fiducialId, objDetectId, objDetectConf, bestCameraToTarget, altCameraToTarget, poseAmbiguity, minAreaRectCorners, detectedCorners` with matching getters incl. `getDetectedObjectClassID()`, `getDetectedObjectConfidence()`. Ships with struct and protobuf serdes (`photonStruct`, `proto`).
landscape.gaps: The 2026 API deprecated `PoseStrategy`, `setPrimaryStrategy`, `setMultiTagFallbackStrategy`, `setReferencePose`, `setLastPose`, and all three `update(...)` overloads (`@Deprecated(forRemoval=true, since="2026")`), replacing them with explicit per-strategy methods — nearly every online 2024/2025 tutorial is now wrong. `estimateConstrainedSolvepnpPose` and `estimateRioMultiTagPose` require you to hand in `cameraMatrix`/`distCoeffs` yourself from `camera.getCameraMatrix()`/`getDistCoeffs()`, both `Optional`. Requires per-resolution calibration or 3D mode silently refuses to work. No built-in gyro-fused ambiguity-free mode equivalent to MegaTag2 except `PNP_DISTANCE_TRIG_SOLVE`/`CONSTRAINED_SOLVEPNP`, which need `addHeadingData()` fed every loop.
landscape.version2026: v2026.3.4 (2026-04-10) is latest stable; v2026.1.1 (2026-01-22) was the first full release (Vue 3 UI, dark mode, Rubik Pi 3 object detection, NT metrics publishing, new pose strategies, Limelight 4 hardware support); v2026.2.1 added 2026 FUEL detection models, max targets raised to 127, OV9281 autoexposure fix. v2027.0.0-alpha-2 exists (2026-05-27). NOTE: user is pinned to 2026.1.1 and should move to 2026.3.4.

landscape.doesWell: The only production-grade FRC camera sim: renders tag corners through real intrinsics + distortion, injects per-pixel noise, models FPS/exposure/latency distributions, and drives the *real* `PhotonCamera` NT topics so your production code path is exercised unchanged. `VisionSystemSim(String label)` with `addAprilTags(AprilTagFieldLayout)`, `addVisionTargets(VisionTargetSim...)`, `addCamera(PhotonCameraSim, Transform3d)`, `adjustCamera(PhotonCameraSim, Transform3d)`, `update(Pose3d|Pose2d)`, `Field2d getDebugField()`. `PhotonCameraSim(PhotonCamera, SimCameraProperties)` (and a 3-arg overload taking the tag layout), `enableRawStream(boolean)`, `enableProcessedStream(boolean)`, `enableDrawWireframe(boolean)`. `SimCameraProperties`: ctors `()`, `(String path,int w,int h)`, `(Path,int,int)` reading a real PhotonVision `config.json`; factories `PERFECT_90DEG()`, `PI4_LIFECAM_320_240()`, `PI4_LIFECAM_640_480()`, `LL2_640_480()`, `LL2_960_720()`, `LL2_1280_720()`; setters `setRandomSeed(long)`, `setCalibration(int,int,Rotation2d)`, `setCalibration(int,int,Matrix camIntrinsics,Matrix distCoeffs)`, `setCalibError(double avgErrorPx,double stdDevPx)`, `setFPS(double)`, `setExposureTimeMs(double)`, `setAvgLatencyMs(double)`, `setLatencyStdDevMs(double)`. `VisionTargetSim(Pose3d, TargetModel)` and `VisionTargetSim(Pose3d, TargetModel, int classId, float confidence)` for simulated object detection. `TargetModel.kAprilTag36h11` etc.
landscape.gaps: Presets stop at Limelight 2 — no LL3G/LL4/OV9281 preset. Simulating a Limelight requires wrapping it in a fake `PhotonCamera`, which PumpkinLib should do transparently. No simulated MegaTag2 behavior (no gyro-fused ambiguity resolution), so sim is slightly optimistic vs a real LL4.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib ships `PumpkinCameraProps` presets built on `SimCameraProperties`: `OV9281_1280_800_82DEG()`, `OV9281_640_400_82DEG()` (LL4/LL3G), `OV5647_640_480_54DEG()` (LL3A), `ARDUCAM_OV2311_1600_1200()`. Every `VisionCameraIO` implementation gets a paired `*Sim` that registers into a single process-wide `VisionSystemSim`, so sim is one boolean, not a rewrite.

landscape.doesWell: This is the de-facto reference vendor-agnostic vision layer and PumpkinLib should treat it as the baseline to beat. It defines `VisionIO` with `@AutoLog VisionIOInputs { boolean connected; TargetObservation latestTargetObservation; PoseObservation[] poseObservations; int[] tagIds; }`, `record TargetObservation(Rotation2d tx, Rotation2d ty)`, `record PoseObservation(double timestamp, Pose3d pose, double ambiguity, int tagCount, double averageTagDistance, PoseObservationType type)`, `enum PoseObservationType { MEGATAG_1, MEGATAG_2, PHOTONVISION }`, and `@FunctionalInterface VisionConsumer { void accept(Pose2d, double timestampSeconds, Matrix<N3,N1> stdDevs); }`. Implementations: `VisionIOLimelight(String name, Supplier<Rotation2d> rotationSupplier)`, `VisionIOPhotonVision(String name, Transform3d robotToCamera)`, `VisionIOPhotonVisionSim(String name, Transform3d, Supplier<Pose2d>)`. Verbatim rejection filter: reject if `tagCount==0`, or `tagCount==1 && ambiguity>maxAmbiguity(0.3)`, or `abs(pose.getZ())>maxZError(0.75)`, or pose outside `[0, layout.getFieldLength()] x [0, layout.getFieldWidth()]`. Verbatim std-dev model: `stdDevFactor = pow(averageTagDistance,2)/tagCount; linear = 0.02*factor; angular = 0.06*factor;` then `*= 0.5` linear and `*= POSITIVE_INFINITY` angular for MEGATAG_2, then `*= cameraStdDevFactors[i]`. Logs `TagPoses`, `RobotPoses`, `RobotPosesAccepted`, `RobotPosesRejected` per camera plus a `Vision/Summary` table. Uses FPGA timestamps throughout so estimates go straight into a WPILib pose estimator with no CTRE `Utils.fpgaToCurrentTime()` conversion.
landscape.gaps: No object-detection path. No custom/NT-raw source. Rejection is a hardcoded boolean expression, not a pluggable chain, and rejected poses lose their reason. Std-dev model is hardcoded. Limelight has no sim implementation. No drive-to-pose / aim commands. No tag-layout override loading (WPIcal output). Single global `aprilTagLayout` static, so you cannot A/B a calibrated layout at runtime. `VisionIOLimelight` calls `NetworkTableInstance.getDefault().flush()` every loop (their own comment: "Increases network traffic but recommended by Limelight").
landscape.version2026: AdvantageKit 2026 (WPILib 2026 support). CAUTION: the `main` branch template source is already written against WPILib 2027 packages (`org.wpilib.math.geometry.*`, `org.wpilib.wpilibj.*`) and uses `RobotController.getMonotonicTime()`; the 2026 release template uses `edu.wpi.first.*`.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib's `VisionCameraIO`/`VisionFrame` should be a strict superset of `VisionIO`/`PoseObservation` so a team can port an AdvantageKit template project by changing imports only. Keep `@AutoLog` on the inputs class and keep the `VisionConsumer` functional-interface signature identical.

landscape.doesWell: `SwerveDrivePoseEstimator(SwerveDriveKinematics, Rotation2d gyroAngle, SwerveModulePosition[], Pose2d initialPose)` and a 6-arg overload adding `Matrix<N3,N1> stateStdDevs, Matrix<N3,N1> visionMeasurementStdDevs`. Inherited from `PoseEstimator`: `addVisionMeasurement(Pose2d, double timestampSeconds)`, `addVisionMeasurement(Pose2d, double, Matrix<N3,N1>)`, `setVisionMeasurementStdDevs(Matrix<N3,N1>)`, `getEstimatedPosition()`, `resetPose(Pose2d)`, `resetPosition(Rotation2d, T wheelPositions, Pose2d)`, `resetRotation(Rotation2d)`, `resetTranslation(Translation2d)`, `Pose2d sampleAt(double timestamp)`, `update(Rotation2d, T)`, plus `updateWithTime(double, Rotation2d, SwerveModulePosition[])`. `sampleAt(double)` is the key primitive for latency-compensated aiming and for gyro-disagreement rejection. `AprilTagFieldLayout`: ctors `(String path)`, `(Path)`, `(List<AprilTag>, double fieldLength, double fieldWidth)`; `static loadField(AprilTagFields)`, `static loadFromResource(String)`, `getTags()`, `getTagPose(int)->Optional<Pose3d>`, `getFieldLength()`, `getFieldWidth()`, `setOrigin(OriginPosition|Pose3d)`, `getOrigin()`, `serialize(String|Path)`. `AprilTagFields` constants: `k2022RapidReact, k2023ChargedUp, k2024Crescendo, k2025ReefscapeWelded, k2025ReefscapeAndyMark, k2026RebuiltWelded, k2026RebuiltAndymark, kDefaultField`; `loadAprilTagLayoutField()` is deprecated in favor of `AprilTagFieldLayout.loadField(...)`.
landscape.gaps: `addVisionMeasurement` silently no-ops if the timestamp falls outside the internal odometry buffer (default 1.5s) — a disconnected/badly-timestamped camera produces zero visible error. No built-in outlier rejection, no std-dev model, no logging of accepted/rejected. `AprilTagFieldLayout` has no merge/override helper for a WPIcal-corrected layout. `setOrigin` is a mutable global on a shared object — a classic footgun when two subsystems hold the same layout instance.
landscape.version2026: WPILib 2026.2.2 (allwpilib release docs). 2027 preview: packages renamed `edu.wpi.first.*` -> `org.wpilib.*`, C++ `frc::` -> `wpi::`; NT3 support removed; `robotInit()` removed; PoseEstimator math changed to scale transforms instead of twists; new `ChassisAccelerations`; Java 25 / Systemcore.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib wraps the estimator so teams never call `addVisionMeasurement` directly: `PumpkinPoseEstimator.registerVisionSource(VisionSource)` + `.setOdometry(...)`, with an internal buffer-age guard that raises a WPILib `Alert` when a source's timestamps are older than the odometry buffer.

landscape.doesWell: Two-stage tool. Stage 1: camera intrinsics from a ChArUco video (5x5 ArUco dictionary), solvable with OpenCV or mrcal backends (mrcal recommended), producing `cameracalibration.json`. Stage 2: field calibration — film field tags from many angles with the same camera, supply an ideal field-map JSON as reference, designate one 'pinned' tag as ground truth, and it optimizes all other tag poses relative to it. Outputs both a WPILib-format `.json` layout and a Limelight `.fmap`. Field-agnostic; supports custom layouts and combining multiple partial field calibrations. Includes a visualizer showing per-tag meter/degree deltas vs the ideal layout.
landscape.gaps: Docs are explicit: 'not a silver bullet' — it only corrects minor placement error and only pays off for teams that already do everything else right. Tags must start approximately correct. Requires video capture discipline (Linux users must transcode to MJPEG .avi). No official guidance on doing this at a competition event in a 20-minute window, and no automated pipeline to push the result to both robot code and coprocessors.
landscape.version2026: Ships with WPILib 2026; docs reference field JSON at allwpilib v2026.2.1 as the recommended reference layout. WPILib stated for the 2026 release they anticipated most features unchanged from 2025.
landscape.integrationShape:
PumpkinLib should NOT rebuild this. Instead ship a loader + deploy convention:
```java
public static AprilTagFieldLayout resolveLayout(AprilTagFields fallback) // deploy/pumpkin/field-layout.json wins if present
public static AprilTagFieldLayout mergeOverride(AprilTagFieldLayout base, Path overrideJson) // per-tag override, logs deltas
```
plus a `FieldLayoutHealth` logger that records, for every accepted frame, the residual between the observed tag pose and the layout tag pose so a team can *see* which tag is miscalibrated during a practice match.

landscape.doesWell: Rigorous camera-model calibration with uncertainty quantification and splined lens models; catches the failure mode where OpenCV reports sub-pixel reprojection error but the model is still badly wrong at the image periphery (exactly where distant tags land). Integrated as an optional backend inside both PhotonVision's calibration flow and WPIcal.
landscape.gaps: Linux/WSL2 only for the deep-dive tooling; PhotonVision exposes it via a `calibrationUtils.py` helper that extracts snapshots and emits VNL files. Steep learning curve; not something a rookie team will operate.
landscape.version2026: Available as a calibration backend in PhotonVision 2026 and WPIcal 2026
landscape.integrationShape: Documentation + a `pumpkin calib check` CLI/dashboard widget that ingests a PhotonVision calibration JSON and flags: mean reprojection error > 1.0 px, computed FOV differing from datasheet by > 10°, or fewer than ~12 snapshots. No code integration needed.

landscape.tool: Custom coprocessor pipelines: Northstar (6328), GompeiVision (Team 190), CubVision (1701)
landscape.doesWell: Northstar is the reference homebrew design: Python + OpenCV ArUco on Orange Pi 5, one process per camera, publishing raw `double[]` frames over NT4 with `PubSubOption.keepDuplicates(true), sendAll(true), pollStorage(5), periodic(0.01)` so the RIO gets *every* frame with a real NT server timestamp, not a 50Hz snapshot. Config is pushed *down* from robot code over NT (`<device>/config/camera_id, camera_resolution_width/height, camera_auto_exposure, camera_exposure, camera_gain, camera_denoise, camera_balance_red/blue, fiducial_size_m, tag_layout, throttle_fps, is_recording, event_name, match_type, match_number, timestamp`) so all vision config is version-controlled in the robot repo. Outputs on `<device>/output/observations` (double[]), `objdetect_observations` (double[]), `fps_apriltags`, `fps_objdetect` (int). Supports on-camera match recording gated on FMS attachment, and per-camera `stdDevFactor` + tunable pitch fudge factors.
landscape.gaps: No web UI, no calibration UI, no packaging — you build and flash your own image. Wire format is positional and self-invented (see integrationShape), so nothing else can read it. Requires a Python + OpenCV toolchain competency most small teams don't have. Not a product: 6328 publish it, they don't support it.
landscape.integrationShape:
Northstar 2026 wire format, decoded from `Vision.java` + `vision_types.py`:
- `observations` double[]: `[0]=poseCount (0,1,2)`. If 1 (multi-tag): `[1]=error0, [2..4]=x,y,z, [5..8]=quaternion(w,x,y,z)`, tag blocks start at index 9. If 2 (single tag, both PnP solutions): `[1]=error0, [2..8]=pose0`, `[9]=error1, [10..16]=pose1`, tag blocks start at index 17. Tag blocks are stride 10: `tag_id, 8 corner angles (tx,ty x4), distance`. Poses are CAMERA poses in field space; robot pose = `cameraPose.transformBy(robotToCamera.inverse())`.
- `objdetect_observations` double[] (read as float[]): stride 10 per detection: `class_id, confidence, then 4 (tx,ty) corner-angle pairs`. In 2026 class 0 = FUEL, class 1 = ROBOT.
PumpkinLib should adopt a *versioned, struct-serialized* successor of this (see capabilities) rather than a positional double array, but must ship a `NorthstarSchema` decoder so teams can drop in existing Northstar/CubVision/GompeiVision coprocessors unchanged.

landscape.doesWell: Official Raspberry Pi image with OpenCV, cscore, ntcore, robotpy-cscore, pyntcore and Java 17 preinstalled, plus a web console for camera config and a sample vision program in C++/Java/Python. Lowest-friction way to get a custom OpenCV pipeline onto the robot network.
landscape.gaps: No AprilTag pipeline, no calibration UI, no pose solving, no object detection — it is a blank canvas. Effectively superseded by PhotonVision for anything tag-related. Pi 3B/4 tested; performance is inadequate for high-res AprilTag work. Teams that go this route almost always end up reimplementing timestamping badly.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should ship a `pumpkin-vision-py` pip package (thin) that any WPILibPi/Orange Pi/Jetson script imports to publish in the PumpkinLib schema with correct timestamps — the value is the wire contract, not the image.

landscape.doesWell: `AutoBuilder.pathfindToPose(Pose2d targetPose, PathConstraints constraints, double goalEndVelocity)` produces an on-the-fly obstacle-avoiding command to any pose — the natural back half of 'see tag -> drive to scoring pose'. Also `pathfindThenFollowPath(PathPlannerPath, PathConstraints)`.
landscape.gaps: Requires `AutoBuilder.configure(...)` to have been called. Pathfinding is field-obstacle aware but not vision-aware — it will happily path to a pose derived from a bad vision estimate. Rotation/rotation-delay is ignored on non-holonomic drivetrains. It is the wrong tool for the last 30cm of an alignment; teams pair it with a direct PID/profiled controller for terminal approach.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib's `AlignCommands.driveToPose(...)` should be a two-phase composition: `AutoBuilder.pathfindToPose(target, constraints, endVel)` while distance > handoffMeters, then hand off to an internal `ProfiledPIDController x/y + theta` terminal controller with a vision-freshness gate, so the robot never blindly finishes an alignment on a 500ms-stale pose.

landscape.doesWell: Full OpenCV + numpy inside the camera, sandboxed, hot-reloaded with errors printed in the web UI. Signature is `def runPipeline(image, llrobot):` returning `(largestContour, image, llpython)` — the contour drives automatic crosshair targeting, the image is what you see in the stream, and `llpython` is a number array surfaced on the `llpython` NT key. Robot->camera data goes the other way via the `llrobot` NT number array. This is the escape hatch for game-specific logic (custom gamepiece geometry, color+shape fusion, per-tag heuristics) without a separate coprocessor. 2026 adds an AI SnapScript generator at the docs site.
landscape.gaps: Python on the Limelight CPU is slow relative to the native pipelines — it competes with AprilTag processing for the same cores. `llrobot`/`llpython` are untyped double arrays with no schema, so contract drift between robot code and script is a live hazard. No debugger, no unit test path.
landscape.integrationShape: PumpkinLib should provide a typed codec over `llrobot`/`llpython`: `SnapScriptChannel.of(name).outbound(RobotStatePacket::pack).inbound(MyResult::unpack)` with a matching Python-side helper so the array layout is declared once. Also expose `LimelightHelpers.setPythonScriptData/getPythonScriptData` behind it.

capabilities.capability: `VisionFrame` — one immutable vendor-neutral observation record that every source produces
capabilities.whyItMatters: A small team cannot afford to rewrite its pose-estimation logic when it swaps a Limelight for a PhotonVision Orange Pi mid-season, or when a camera dies at an event and the only spare is a different brand. One record type means the filter chain, the std-dev model, the logging, the replay and the dashboard are written once and work for all three vendors plus sim. This is the single highest-leverage thing in the whole domain.
capabilities.prerequisites: None. Do this first; everything else depends on it.

capabilities.capability: `VisionCameraIO` + `@AutoLog` inputs, with Limelight / PhotonVision / Custom-NT / Sim implementations
capabilities.whyItMatters: AdvantageKit-style IO layers are what make a small team's vision system debuggable: every frame that entered the robot is in the log, so a bad pose at a competition can be replayed on a laptop that night and the fix verified without the field. The user already runs AdvantageKit, so this must be `@AutoLog`-native, not bolted on. Crucially it must also work *without* AdvantageKit for teams that don't use it.
capabilities.prerequisites: VisionFrame; a `VisionFrameStruct` implementing `edu.wpi.first.util.struct.Struct<VisionFrame>` so AdvantageKit can log frames without flattening to parallel arrays.

capabilities.capability: Pluggable filter chain with named reject reasons, replacing the hardcoded boolean
capabilities.whyItMatters: The AdvantageKit template's filter is one boolean expression; when a small team's robot teleports at an event they get no signal about *why*. A filter chain that records a `RejectReason` per frame, logs a per-reason counter, and surfaces a dashboard histogram converts 'vision is broken' into 'camera 2 rejected 340 frames for GYRO_DISAGREEMENT in match 14' — which a student can act on. This is the difference between a small team debugging in the pit and a small team giving up on vision.
capabilities.prerequisites: VisionFrame; access to `SwerveDrivePoseEstimator.sampleAt(double)` for gyro-disagreement and pose-jump checks.

capabilities.capability: Pluggable standard-deviation model with the three known-good presets built in
capabilities.whyItMatters: Std-dev tuning is where teams' vision quietly fails — the estimator either ignores vision or snaps to it. Shipping the two field-proven models verbatim (AdvantageKit's `d²/n` and 6328's `d²/n²`) with the MegaTag2 angular=∞ rule baked in gives a small team elite-tier behavior on day one, and the interface lets them evolve.

This is the whole thesis. A small team should get multi-camera, multi-vendor, filtered, std-dev-scaled, fully-logged, sim-capable pose estimation from a dozen lines in RobotContainer, and should be able to add a fourth camera of a different brand by adding one line. Every capability above is plumbing; this is the product.

capabilities.capability: Transparent simulation for ALL sources, including Limelight, on one switch
capabilities.whyItMatters: Limelight has no simulation story at all — which means a Limelight team cannot test autos or alignment without a robot and a field, the two things a small team has least of. Wrapping every source in PhotonVision's `VisionSystemSim` (including Limelight, by simulating it as a PhotonCamera and re-encoding the output into the Limelight-shaped `VisionFrame`) is genuinely novel and very high value.
capabilities.prerequisites: photonlib on the classpath (already a dependency); VisionCameraIO. Note limitation: sim will not reproduce MegaTag2's gyro-fused ambiguity resolution, so sim is optimistic — document it.

capabilities.capability: A versioned struct-serialized wire schema for custom coprocessors + a matching Python publisher package
capabilities.whyItMatters: Every homebrew vision system in FRC reinvents a positional double array (Northstar, CubVision, GompeiVision all differ) and every one of them gets timestamping subtly wrong. WPILib 2026 has first-class struct serialization on NetworkTables (`StructPublisher`/`StructArrayPublisher`, `Struct<T>` with 'struct:' type strings) — nobody has used it to define a *standard* FRC vision wire format. Doing so is the genuine gap in this domain and is cheap to build.
capabilities.prerequisites: VisionFrame + a hand-written `Struct<VisionFrame>` implementation (variable-length target lists need a fixed max-targets cap or a nested struct-array topic). Publish the schema string and version it.

capabilities.capability: Field-layout resolution + live tag-residual health monitoring
capabilities.whyItMatters: Welded-vs-AndyMark layout mismatch is the #1 silent pose bug and it is invisible without instrumentation. And WPIcal output does a team no good if deploying it means hand-editing three places (robot code, PhotonVision UI, Limelight .fmap). Making the layout a single resolved artifact with a visible per-tag residual turns a mystery into a number.

capabilities.capability: Vision-driven action commands: align-to-pose, aim-at-point, auto-intake, shoot-on-the-fly solver
capabilities.whyItMatters: This is the payoff a small team actually sees on the field. Elite teams structure alignment as a two-phase (pathfind then terminal-PID) command with an explicit freshness gate and a tag-id filter; small teams write a `while(tx > 1) turn()` loop that oscillates. Shipping these as composable commands, with the vision freshness/rejection gating already wired, is a direct competitive transfer.
capabilities.prerequisites: PumpkinVision, a Drive interface, PathPlannerLib (optional dependency — degrade to pure terminal control if absent). The shot solver is a fixed-point iteration on time-of-flight; 3-5 iterations converge in practice. Game-specific lookup tables must be team-supplied — PumpkinLib supplies the solver and the tuning UI, not the numbers.

capabilities.whyItMatters: The Limelight Python pipeline is the only way a small team gets custom CV without buying and maintaining a second coprocessor, and today the robot<->script contract is two untyped double arrays that drift silently. A declared codec makes homebrew CV safe for a team with one programmer.

Switching a Limelight pipeline is not instantaneous and there is no documented completion signal; teams read stale targeting data from the previous pipeline for several frames and act on it. A command that switches and waits for `getpipe` to match AND for a fresh heartbeat is a five-line fix for a bug that costs matches.

capabilities.capability: Calibration health checker + a 'why is my vision bad' diagnostic page
capabilities.whyItMatters: The user explicitly wants software that teaches students. The vision analogue of a PID tuner is a diagnostic that says: your calibration reprojection error is 1.8px (should be <1.0), your computed FOV is 63° but your datasheet says 82° (recalibrate), camera 2's frames are arriving 180ms late (check network), tag 7's residual is 9cm (field or layout problem), 41% of camera 1's frames were rejected for HIGH_AMBIGUITY (you are relying on single tags at range).
capabilities.prerequisites: PumpkinVision, TagResidualMonitor, filter chain reject counters

eliteTeamPractices: Read EVERY camera frame, not the latest one. 6328 subscribe with `PubSubOption.keepDuplicates(true), sendAll(true), pollStorage(5), periodic(0.01)` and drain with `readQueue()`; PhotonVision deprecated `getLatestResult()` in favor of `getAllUnreadResults()` for exactly this reason ('can miss results, or provide duplicate ones'). A 120fps camera on a 50Hz loop loses 60% of its data otherwise. Sources: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/VisionIONorthstar.java , https://github.com/PhotonVision/photonvision/blob/v2026.1.1/photon-lib/src/main/java/org/photonvision/PhotonCamera.java

Scale vision standard deviations by distance² and by tag count. AdvantageKit template: `stdDevFactor = pow(avgTagDistance,2)/tagCount`, linear baseline 0.02 m, angular baseline 0.06 rad. 6328's 2026 Darwin code is more aggressive: `xyStdDev = 0.01 * d² / n² * cameraFactor` and `thetaStdDev = 0.03 * d² / n² * cameraFactor` — note n SQUARED, so two tags are 4x more trusted, not 2x. Sources: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/blob/main/template_projects/sources/vision/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/vision/Vision.java , https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/VisionConstants.java

Never let vision correct heading when a gyro is available. 6328 set `thetaStdDev = Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` whenever the observation is a disambiguated single-tag solve; the AdvantageKit template sets `angularStdDevMegatag2Factor = Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY`; Limelight's own docs recommend `VecBuilder.fill(0.7, 0.7, 9999999)` for MegaTag2. Vision heading is the noisiest channel and the one you least need. Sources: https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/pipeline-apriltag/apriltag-robot-localization-megatag2 , https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/Vision.java

Disambiguate single-tag PnP by comparing BOTH solutions against the current gyro heading, rather than trusting the solver's ambiguity ranking. 6328 accept a single-tag frame only when `error0 < error1*0.4 || error1 < error0*0.4` (ambiguityThreshold = 0.4) and then pick whichever of the two candidate robot poses is closer in rotation to `RobotState.getRotation()`. This is strictly better than a plain ambiguity threshold. Source: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/Vision.java

Reject on physics, not just on statistics: field bounds with a margin (6328 use fieldBorderMargin = 0.5 m), Z bounds (6328 use zMin = -0.5, zMax = 1.0 m; AdvantageKit uses |z| < 0.75), and angular rate (Limelight's own MegaTag2 sample rejects when `|gyro.getRate()| > 360` deg/s). A pose that puts the robot 40cm off the floor is wrong regardless of its reported ambiguity. Sources: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/VisionConstants.java , https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/pipeline-apriltag/apriltag-robot-localization-megatag2

Ignore vision for the first seconds of autonomous. 6328 carry `autoIgnoreTimeSecs = 2.0` — during the initial burst of motion the odometry is trustworthy and vision is at its worst (motion blur, tags at extreme angle), and a bad correction in the first second wrecks the whole auto. Source: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/VisionConstants.java

Log accepted AND rejected poses separately, every loop. The AdvantageKit template logs `RobotPoses`, `RobotPosesAccepted`, `RobotPosesRejected` and `TagPoses` per camera plus a Summary table; the entire debugging workflow (drive teleop, watch in AdvantageScope, tune the rejection thresholds) depends on rejected poses being visible rather than dropped. Source: https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/template-projects/vision-template/

Push camera configuration DOWN from robot code, don't configure it in a web UI. 6328's Northstar takes camera id, resolution, exposure, gain, denoise, white balance, fiducial size, tag layout and throttle over NT `config/` topics — so every vision parameter is in git and identical across four coprocessors. Limelight's web-UI-only camera transform is the opposite pattern and is why Limelight teams cannot simulate or replay. Source: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/VisionIONorthstar.java

Model the camera transform as a function of time, not a constant, when a camera is on a moving mechanism. 6328's `CameraConfig.poseFunction` is `Function<Double timestamp, Optional<Pose3d>>` — it returns empty when the mechanism angle at that timestamp is unknown, which correctly drops the frame instead of using a wrong transform. Also note their per-camera `cameraPitchFudgeDegrees` LoggedTunableNumbers (one camera at -4.5°): mounting is never as-CADded. Source: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/VisionConstants.java

Feed the gyro to the camera every single loop and flush NT immediately. MegaTag2 is worthless without it. The AdvantageKit Limelight IO writes `robot_orientation_set` then calls `NetworkTableInstance.getDefault().flush()` with the comment 'Increases network traffic but recommended by Limelight'. On LL4, prefer IMU mode 4 (INTERNAL_EXTERNAL_ASSIST) so the internal IMU carries you between external updates. Sources: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/blob/main/template_projects/sources/vision/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/vision/VisionIOLimelight.java , https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/pipeline-apriltag/apriltag-robot-localization-megatag2

Calibrate at the exact resolution you will run, with a ChArUco board, and check the numbers. PhotonVision docs: calibration is specific to each physical camera AND each resolution; mean reprojection error should be under ~1 px; computed FOV should match the datasheet within ±10°; take at least 12 images at varying distances and up to 45° tilts; mount the board rigidly and flat, never handheld; print at 100% and measure the printed markers with calipers. Prefer the mrcal backend over OpenCV. Source: https://docs.photonvision.org/en/latest/docs/calibration/calibration.html

Calibrate the FIELD, not just the camera, once everything else is right. WPIcal measures real tag positions relative to a pinned reference tag and emits both a WPILib layout JSON and a Limelight .fmap. WPILib is explicit that this yields limited benefit and only for teams that have already done everything else correctly — so it is the last optimization, not the first. Source: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/wpical/index.html

Run object detection as tx/ty corner observations, not as poses. 6328's 2026 object pipeline publishes, per detection, `class_id, confidence, and the four corner (tx,ty) angle pairs` — the robot code then projects onto the ground plane using the known camera transform. This is far more robust than trusting a coprocessor's 3D estimate of a sphere. They also explicitly track opposing ROBOTS as class 1 alongside game pieces as class 0. Source: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/Vision.java

Alert loudly when a camera goes quiet. Both 6328's Vision subsystem (a 1.5 s disconnect timer plus a separate NT-connection check, distinguishing 'connected to NT but not publishing frames' from 'disconnected from NT') and the AdvantageKit template raise WPILib `Alert`s. A silently dead camera degrades pose estimation invisibly. Source: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/Vision.java

Record match video on the camera, gated on FMS attachment. 6328 debounce `DriverStation.isFMSAttached()` by 3 s and push `is_recording` to every Northstar; Limelight OS 2026 ships Rewind on LL4 (always-buffering, zero disk cost until saved, .rwnd bundles synchronized video + targeting + hardware + config, ~500µs-1ms latency penalty). Post-match video of what the camera actually saw is how elite teams resolve 'the robot went the wrong way'. Sources: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2026Public/blob/main/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2026/subsystems/vision/Vision.java , https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/software-change-log

Throttle vision when you need CPU elsewhere. 6328 push `throttle_fps` to every camera based on a global `Robot.shouldThrottle()`; Limelight exposes `throttle_set` (skip N frames between processed frames, also for thermal control) and `fiducial_downscale_set`. Source: https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/apis/complete-networktables-api

Use `PoseEstimator.sampleAt(double timestamp)` rather than the current pose when you need the robot pose that corresponds to a vision frame or a shot. It is the only correct way to compare a vision heading against the gyro heading at capture time, and the only correct way to aim at a latency-compensated target. Source: https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/math/estimator/SwerveDrivePoseEstimator.html

For shoot-on-the-fly, move the target, not the robot: subtract `v_robot * timeOfFlight` from the goal position and re-solve, iterating because time-of-flight depends on the corrected range. Requires a turret or a swerve that can rotate independently of translation. Expect the flywheel/hood setpoints to be continuously moving, so feedforward-dominant control matters more than tight PID. Source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/advice-on-shooting-while-moving/405472
pitfalls: WELDED vs ANDYMARK layout mismatch. `AprilTagFields.k2026RebuiltWelded` and `k2026RebuiltAndymark` are different fields. PhotonVision ships with the WELDED layout by default; if your robot code loads AndyMark (or vice versa) you get a plausible-looking pose that is wrong by inches to feet, with no error. Verify on BOTH the coprocessor and the roboRIO. https://docs.photonvision.org/en/latest/docs/apriltag-pipelines/multitag.html

MegaTag2 with no gyro feed = garbage. `botpose_orb_wpiblue` is only valid if `robot_orientation_set` / `SetRobotOrientation(name, yaw, 0,0,0,0,0)` is written every frame, blue-origin, CCW-positive, 0° facing the red wall. Writing it once at init produces a pose that looks fine at startup and drifts silently. https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/pipeline-apriltag/apriltag-robot-localization-megatag2

Feeding MegaTag2 the pose estimator's own heading creates a feedback loop. Limelight's sample uses `m_poseEstimator.getEstimatedPosition().getRotation()`, but if vision is also correcting rotation you have a loop. Set angular std dev to infinity (or 9999999) whenever you use MegaTag2, so the gyro is the sole heading authority.

Limelight latency accounting. Total latency for a botpose sample is at index 6 of the array, in MILLISECONDS, and must be subtracted from the NT sample timestamp (in microseconds): `ts = sample.timestamp*1e-6 - value[6]*1e-3`. `tl` (pipeline) and `cl` (capture) are separate NT keys and are NOT the same as index 6. Getting this wrong at 4 m/s shifts your pose by ~20-40 cm. Verified in AdvantageKit `VisionIOLimelight`.
`getBotPoseEstimate_*()` returns only the newest sample. On a 120fps LL4 with a 50Hz loop you throw away over half your frames. Use `readQueue()` on the raw NT topic instead.
`getLatestResults()` (LimelightHelpers) parses the entire JSON dump on the roboRIO. Calling it every loop is a well-known loop-overrun source. Use typed getters or raw NT.

PhotonVision 2026 deprecated the entire `PoseStrategy` path. `PhotonPoseEstimator(layout, strategy, robotToCamera)`, `setPrimaryStrategy`, `setMultiTagFallbackStrategy`, `setReferencePose`, `setLastPose` and all `update(...)` overloads are `@Deprecated(forRemoval=true, since="2026")`. Code copied from 2024/2025 tutorials compiles with warnings today and will break. Use `estimateCoprocMultiTagPose(result)` with an `estimateLowestAmbiguityPose(result)` fallback.

`estimatePnpDistanceTrigSolvePose` and `estimateConstrainedSolvepnpPose` silently do nothing useful without `addHeadingData(timestamp, heading)` being called every loop. `estimateRioMultiTagPose` and `estimateConstrainedSolvepnpPose` also require `camera.getCameraMatrix()` and `camera.getDistCoeffs()`, both `Optional` and both EMPTY if the camera is uncalibrated at the current resolution.

PhotonVision 3D mode requires calibration at the exact streaming resolution. Calibrating at 1280x800 and streaming at 640x400 gives you no 3D output (or wrong output). Recalibrate per resolution. https://docs.photonvision.org/en/latest/docs/calibration/calibration.html

`addVisionMeasurement()` silently no-ops when the timestamp is outside the internal odometry buffer (~1.5 s). A coprocessor whose clock is not NT-synced, or one that publishes wall-clock instead of NT time, produces zero vision correction and zero error messages. Always assert timestamp sanity and log the delta between now and the frame timestamp.

Do not mix time bases. WPILib pose estimators use FPGA time. CTRE Phoenix 6 swerve uses its own 'current time' and requires `Utils.fpgaToCurrentTime()` when feeding `addVisionMeasurement` on a `SwerveDrivetrain`. AdvantageKit's template deliberately uses FPGA timestamps end-to-end so no conversion is needed. Mixing the two produces a constant offset error proportional to speed.

Single-tag coplanar PnP ambiguity flipping. Limelight's own docs: 'If all keypoints are coplanar, there is still some risk of ambiguity flipping.' Their MegaTag1 sample rejects single-tag frames with `ambiguity > 0.7` or `distToCamera > 3` m. AdvantageKit uses `maxAmbiguity = 0.3`. Pick a threshold and also cross-check against gyro heading.

Pose estimation degrades when the camera is normal (perpendicular) to the tag plane — the classic PnP degenerate case. Mount cameras with deliberate yaw/pitch offset rather than staring straight at the tag; 6328 mount at ±70° yaw and 12° pitch. https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/pose-estimation-degrades-when-the-camera-is-normal-to-the-apriltag-plane/514907

Limelight camera-to-robot transform lives in the web UI, not in code. If the camera is reflashed, swapped, or a spare is installed, the transform is gone and every pose is wrong by the mount offset. Push it from robot code with `setCameraPose_RobotSpace` / `camerapose_robotspace_set` at startup, and log what you pushed.

Limelight 4 dropped PoE. It is 5V-26V buck-boost input (3.5V-35V absolute max), 12W max, via a Weidmuller port — you cannot reuse an LL3 PoE injector. https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/getting-started/limelight-4

Limelight OS 2026.0 requirement: wall-mounted tags in 2026 maps will not display correctly until LLOS 2026.0 is installed, and Hailo neural models from the 2026 trainer require LLOS 2026.0. Also, AprilTag acceleration on Hailo was temporarily DISABLED in 2026.0 and returned in 2026.1 (up to 50% faster at 1x downscale). https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/software-change-log

Pipeline switching has real latency and no completion signal. Poll `getpipe`/`getCurrentPipelineIndex` until it matches AND the heartbeat `hb` has advanced before trusting targeting data. UNVERIFIED: the exact settle time is not documented; measure it.

`snapshot` semantics changed in LLOS 2026.0 from a level to a rising-edge counter (0→1→2→3), rate-limited to 1 per 10 frames. Code that sets `snapshot=1` and leaves it will capture once and then stop.

Running OpenCV AprilTag detection on the roboRIO is a trap. WPILib's own vision guidance and every elite team put it on a coprocessor: the RIO's CPU is needed for the 20ms control loop, and tag detection at usable resolution will blow the loop time. Use the RIO only for consuming results. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/vision-processing/introduction/strategies-for-vision-programming.html

Custom-coprocessor timestamping is where homebrew systems die. You must publish MIDDLE-OF-EXPOSURE time (Limelight OS 2026.0 changed to this convention explicitly, using middle-row for rolling shutter) converted into NT server time, not camera monotonic time and not wall clock. If you cannot do this, do not build a custom pipeline.

Rolling shutter (LL3A, LL3, most cheap USB cameras) smears tags under rotation. Global shutter (OV9281 on LL4/LL3G, OV2311 on Arducam) is worth the money for anything moving. PhotonVision docs: 'Global shutter cameras are recommended in all cases.'
PhotonVision does not support Logitech cameras, built-in webcams, or virtual cameras — this bites teams who buy the cheapest USB camera on the shelf.

WPILib 2027 will break every import. `edu.wpi.first.*` becomes `org.wpilib.*`, C++ `frc::` becomes `wpi::`, NT3 is removed, `robotInit()` is removed, and the platform moves to Systemcore/Java 25. AdvantageKit's main-branch templates are ALREADY written against `org.wpilib.*`. PumpkinLib must keep all WPILib types behind a thin internal seam or accept a mechanical rename in Oct 2026. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

AprilTagFieldLayout.setOrigin() mutates a shared object. If two subsystems hold the same layout instance and one flips the origin for red alliance, the other silently sees flipped tag poses. Treat the layout as immutable; use the wpiblue-origin convention everywhere (which is what both vendors emit since 2024).

WPIcal is not magic. WPILib's own docs: it 'is not a silver bullet of computer vision accuracy', it only corrects minor placement error, tags must start approximately correct, and it only pays off after every other localization practice is already right. Do not sell field calibration as a first step.

PathPlanner `pathfindToPose` will happily drive to a pose computed from a stale or rejected vision estimate. Always gate alignment commands on vision freshness and hand off to a terminal controller for the last ~0.5 m.

Object-detection models are game-specific and licensed. PhotonVision's shipped COCO and 2026 FUEL models are AGPLv3 (Ultralytics). PhotonVision explicitly does not support training, only conversion, and object detection is only available on specific hardware (Orange Pi 5 / Rubik Pi 3 as of 2026). Limelight's trainer is free but produces Limelight-format models tied to Hailo 8 / 8L / Coral / CPU runtimes. Do not promise portable models.

PhotonVision 2026.1.1 (the user's pinned version) is the January release; 2026.3.4 (April) is the current stable and includes the FUEL detection models, the 127-target limit raise, and the OV9281 autoexposure fix. Pin bumps matter here.
